faqs.question: How much can I receive in an instant refund advance?
faqs.answer: Qualified clients can receive refund advances ranging from 27,500 ETB up to 412,500 ETB within 24 hours of filing, subject to Ministry of Revenue acceptance and loan approval terms.

faqs.question: Are there any upfront out-of-pocket costs to apply?
faqs.answer: No. There are 0 ETB upfront out-of-pocket fees. Preparation fees and advance repayments can be deducted from your total tax refund.

faqs.question: What documents do I need to bring for tax preparation?
faqs.answer: Please bring a valid government-issued ID, national ID or TIN, employment income statements, other income records, direct deposit account info, and any applicable deduction forms.

faqs.question: How does the 2,750 ETB referral bonus work?
faqs.answer: For every new client you refer who completes tax preparation with us, you receive a 2750B ETBonus with no limit on referrals.

faqs.question: Do you assist with Ministry of Revenue audit protection and back taxes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our certified tax preparers provide Ministry of Revenue audit representation, back-tax resolution, and penalty abatement support.

newsPosts.title: Holiday Advances are open — no fee, up to 27,500 ETB
newsPosts.excerpt: Eligible clients can take a no-fee Holiday Advance through the filing deadline. Bring your documents and pre-qualify today.
newsPosts.body:
Holiday Advances start in the season and run through the filing deadline. There is no Bole Revenue Desk fee on this product. Eligibility depends on income, filing status, and a complete document set.

If you need a larger amount, ask about Shield Advances from 27,500 ETB to 412,500 ETB. We will show bank fees before anything is processed.

blogPosts.title: A guide for income tax preparation & advances
blogPosts.excerpt: What Holiday and Shield Advances are, what to bring, and how repayment works when the Ministry of Revenue pays.
blogPosts.body:
Tax refund advances are short-term funds against a completed return. Holiday Advances carry no Bole Revenue Desk fee. Shield Advances range from 27,500 ETB to 412,500 ETB and may include bank fees.

Bring ID, TINs, employment income statements or pay stubs, and dependent documents. After we file, approved clients can take an advance. The Ministry of Revenue refund later repays the advance and any disclosed fees automatically.

You can always say no and wait for the full refund.
blogPosts.author: E. Bel

blogPosts.title: Information about referral program and bonuses
blogPosts.excerpt: How existing clients earn when family and friends file with The Bole Revenue Desk.
blogPosts.body:
Tell your people to mention your name at intake. After their return is filed, you receive the posted referral bonus. There is no charge to the person you send.

Ask your preparer for this season’s amount. Bonuses are one of the ways we thank clients who keep the waiting room full.
blogPosts.author: The Bole Revenue Desk Team

blogPosts.title: How to find the right business tax preparation & audit support
blogPosts.excerpt: Schedule C and 1120 filings, plus a safety net if the Ministry of Revenue writes. Existing clients are not charged for audit support.
blogPosts.body:
Gather income statements, expenses, and receipts. Use the right form — Schedule C for sole proprietors, 1120 for corporations — and bring it to the preparer.

We file for the business and stay on the file if an audit starts. Existing Bole Revenue Desk clients are not charged for audit support. That is the safety net.
blogPosts.author: E. Bel
